utility.notes: AES Indiana is Indianapolis's well-established dominant electric utility, confirmed directly by the City's own permitting checklist (which names AES Indiana specifically for interconnection).

value.name: AES Indiana
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Indianapolis's residential solar customers this session; AES Indiana is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

county.notes: Indianapolis and Marion County operate a consolidated city-county government (Unigov); the Department of Business and Neighborhood Services (DBNS) is the single permitting authority for the whole consolidated jurisdiction.

permit_authority.value: Indianapolis-Marion County Department of Business and Neighborhood Services (DBNS)
permit_authority.notes: Indiana's building code is adopted statewide by the Indiana Fire Prevention and Building Safety Commission (currently the 2020 Indiana Residential Code, with electrical chapters referencing the 2017 National Electrical Code), but enforcement is local. Indianapolis-Marion County's own DBNS is a genuinely consolidated authority for the whole city-county (Unigov) jurisdiction — the same efficient pattern as Louisville/Jefferson County, KY, researched separately this session.

interconnection_url.notes: Per AES Indiana's own page: two programs apply depending on installation date. Existing 'Net Metering' (Rider 9) covers systems installed before 2022-06-30, with credits based on net energy usage and indefinite rollover during participation. 'Rate EDG' (Rider 16, Excess Distributed Generation) applies to systems installed on/after 2022-06-30, crediting excess generation financially rather than through retail-rate net metering — currently 3.935 cents/kWh sent back to AES Indiana. Interconnection tiers: Level 1 (systems ≤10kW, no fee) and Level 2 (10kW-2MW, $50 + $1/kW fee); net metering itself caps eligible systems at 1MW. Inverters must be IEEE 1547-2018 and UL 1741 certified; AES Indiana installs a bidirectional meter after approval.

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own 'Solar Photovoltaic Systems Required Documents Checklist' (Office of Sustainability). Applicants must also comply with any applicable private deed restrictions or HOA covenants, which the City does not itself enforce. A resubmittal for incomplete/deficient documentation is treated as a new application, processed in order of receipt.

value: Foundation (if applicable — typically not for a rooftop-mount system)
inspection_steps.notes: Per DBNS's own 'Schedule of Requirements — Inspections and Closeout' document (last updated 2026-01-02), the general Building inspection sequence lists Foundation, Under Slab, Framing, Rough (Electrical/Plumbing/Mechanical), and Final (Electrical/Plumbing/Mechanical) — this is the general construction inspection sequence, not solar-specific; for a typical rooftop-mount residential solar installation with no new foundation or framing work, only the Rough Electrical and Final Electrical steps would typically apply.
